name: Alberta
note: Alberta's long-running everyday plate is white with red characters and the slogan "Wild Rose Country"; a new "Strong and Free" plate with a Moraine Lake panorama, picked by public vote in November 2025, was due to start issuing in mid-2026.

name: British Columbia
note: B.C.'s everyday plate is white with blue characters, a setting-sun flag emblem in the middle and the slogan "Beautiful British Columbia" along the bottom.

name: Manitoba
note: Manitoba's everyday plate reads "Friendly Manitoba", and drivers can also choose a bilingual version that says "Bienvenue".

name: New Brunswick
note: New Brunswick's everyday plate is white with dark lettering and the provincial emblem; no official picture was found on gnb.ca.

name: Newfoundland and Labrador
note: Newfoundland and Labrador's everyday plates start with A, H, J, C or M, and since 2023 the province has stopped using renewal stickers.

name: Nova Scotia
note: Nova Scotia's everyday plate was recently redesigned for visibility: the painted border and left sticker well are gone and every plate type now uses a single font.

name: Ontario
note: Ontario's everyday plate is white with blue lettering, a crown, and the slogan "Yours to Discover"; a short-lived blue "A Place to Grow" design was dropped in 2020.

name: Prince Edward Island
note: PEI refreshed its plate in late 2022 with a simple, high-visibility design as it moved to 6-digit numbers, and added a distinct plate for electric vehicles.

name: Quebec
note: Quebec's plate is white with blue characters and the provincial motto "Je me souviens" ("I remember"), which has been on its plates since 1978.

name: Saskatchewan
note: Saskatchewan's everyday plate carries the slogan "Land of Living Skies" in green on white.

name: Northwest Territories
note: The NWT's famous polar-bear-shaped plate dates to 1970, when Commissioner Stuart Hodgson designed it for the territory's centennial, and it still fits the standard 6-by-12-inch plate size.

name: Nunavut
note: In 2025 Nunavut brought back a polar-bear-shaped plate, inspired by the territory's 25th anniversary, and began issuing it in September 2025.

name: Yukon
note: Yukon's everyday plate is famous for its Klondike gold-rush prospector.
